### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the elapsed time between consecutive completions of A02 and A07 was about 0.86 hours on average (median about 0.88 hours, typical range roughly 0.78–0.93 hours); in the later window it was about 0.43 hours on average (median about 0.44 hours, typical range roughly 0.37–0.48 hours) — a reduction of about 0.43 hours, close to half. [TWAIT001]
- The spread of these gaps narrowed only slightly (standard deviation about 0.09 hours before versus about 0.07 hours after), so the shift is a broadly uniform reduction across cases rather than a change in variability alone. [TWAIT001]
- This gap is observed in only a minority of traces: about 16 in 100 traces in the earlier window and about 18 in 100 in the later window (32 and 35 of 200 traces). [TWAIT001]
- The size of the timing difference is unusual for a random split — all but about 1 of 2000 random re-splits of the pooled traces showed a smaller difference — but it is a single item on one activity pair. [TWAIT001]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. Only one time item qualified (against roughly 0.01 expected by chance in the time family, with no control-flow items among 55 units where about 0.27 were expected), and a single item when fewer than one is expected is what an unchanged process typically produces however unusual it looks — particularly here, where the A02–A07 gap is observed in only about a sixth of traces, so sampling variation in a minority of cases cannot be ruled out. [TWAIT001]
